purpose: How a working gold-plating bench chooses the right gold bath system for a job: which family (alkaline cyanide, acid hard gold, sulfite non-cyanide, electroless/immersion) and which strike, build and color roles plus support baths fit the substrate, wear class, color and karat target, forming sequence, shop hazard readiness and regulated-claim context — always governed by the commercial product's technical data sheet, proven on a coupon, and recorded before any customer piece enters a tank.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

operating setpoints (temperature, pH, gold concentration, current density, time) belong to the technical data sheet of the specific commercial product; this KB teaches what each parameter class does and may cite published handbook-class ranges only AS ranges, never as universal setpoints
the shop runs purchased commercial plating chemistry per its TDS; no bath is formulated from raw chemicals

wherever cyanide-bearing and acid tanks both exist, they are physically and procedurally segregated — separate zones, separate storage, separate drains — and operators hold the formal training their jurisdiction requires

regulated marking terms (gold plated, vermeil, gold filled), nickel-release limits and waste rules are obligation classes whose current numeric thresholds are verified in the selling jurisdiction before any claim is made
exclusions: in-service bath control: what concentration, pH, temperature, agitation and additive drift do over a bath's working weeks, drift signatures, titration/Hull-cell/coupon-XRF/supplier-lab analysis routines, replenishment discipline and the bath log — the territory of the sibling KB 'Bath Analysis, Control & Replenishment'

contamination and end-of-life: drag-in/drag-out control, metallic and organic contamination signatures, filtration and carbon treatment, bath aging, regenerate-vs-replace economics and gold recovery from spent solutions — the territory of the sibling KB 'Contamination Control & Bath Lifecycle'
executing the run: rectifier setup, current density delivery, surface-area estimation, racking and fixturing, layer-stack execution and run logging (the process-execution specialist's domain)
surface preparation, substrate triage of customer pieces, and mechanical finishing before plate (the surface-prep specialist's domain)
final color-match acceptance against a customer reference, defect diagnosis on finished work and rework routing (the quality-finish specialist's domain)

invented numeric setpoints, prices, or wear-life guarantees stated as fact; every such figure is either a mechanism, a published handbook-class range cited as a range, or a verify-by-TDS/measurement instruction
DIY bath formulation from raw chemicals or salts, including compounding cyanide or gold-sulfite solutions from precursors
PVD and other dry-coating process design — PVD is named only as an out-of-scope alternative class a job may be referred to
personalized legal, medical or financial advice; nickel-allergy and chemical-exposure questions route to regulation classes, formal training and professional care

competency_questions.question: Which gold bath family fits this job — how do I decide between alkaline cyanide, acid hard gold, sulfite non-cyanide and the electroless/immersion class?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the four family nodes each state what the family deposits, its defining strength, its defining liability and its hazard tier, and SELECTION_RECORD_GATE shows how the choice is committed

competency_questions.question: What must the job profile capture before any bath family is even named?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JOB_REQUIREMENTS_PROFILE lists substrate identity, wear class, color/karat target, forming sequence, quantity, skin-contact/compliance context and customer expectation as the mandatory selection inputs

competency_questions.question: Where do my operating setpoints come from, and what is this KB allowed to tell me about temperature, pH, gold content and current density?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TDS_DOCTRINE states that the specific commercial product's technical data sheet governs setpoints, that this KB teaches parameter mechanisms and handbook-class ranges only, and that a solution without a TDS is not selectable

competency_questions.question: What must be true of my shop before a cyanide-bearing gold family is even on the selection menu?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HAZARD_TIER_GATE names the readiness classes (segregation, storage, ventilation and monitoring, training, emergency readiness, jurisdiction licensing check) that gate cyanide-tier families, and states the never-mix cyanide/acid line

competency_questions.question: What is a gold strike for, how does it differ from a build bath and a color bath, and when can a strike be skipped?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOLD_STRIKE_ROLE explains adhesion insurance against displacement deposition plus the sacrificial contamination-buffer role, and STRIKE_COLOR_BUILD_ARCHITECTURE maps jobs onto the three roles with the rule for when each is required

competency_questions.question: How do I shift the deposit's hue toward rose, yellow or green, and what does alloying do to the effective karat of the coat?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COLOR_KARAT_ALLOYING names the alloying mechanism per hue direction (copper toward rose, silver toward green, nickel toward pale, cobalt slightly rose) and states that alloy content lowers effective karat of the coating

competency_questions.question: Which support baths — nickel, copper, palladium — does my job need, and what does each class actually do under the gold?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPORT_BATH_CLASSES describes nickel (bright vs sulfamate, with the nickel-release compliance flag), copper (strike and leveling) and palladium (nickel-free barrier) as classes with the job situations that call for each

competency_questions.question: Why can gold never go straight onto steel or stainless, and what stack does each substrate class demand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBSTRATE_MATCH explains displacement (immersion) deposition and iron poisoning as the mechanisms, and maps substrate classes (steel, stainless, brass/copper, silver, zinc die-cast) to their activation-strike and barrier requirements

competency_questions.question: The customer wants to bend or size the piece after plating — how does that change which gold system I may select?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORM_SEQUENCE_DECISION states that hardened acid golds are brittle and crack on post-forming, that soft golds are the only class with a limited plate-then-form allowance, and that form-first is the default production order

competency_questions.question: What will a candidate selection cost in locked-up gold and expected bath life, and how do family efficiency and rate classes change tank time?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOLD_INVENTORY_BATHLIFE gives the inventory mechanism (volume times concentration locks gold capital) and family bath-life classes, and EFFICIENCY_RATE_CLASS compares cathode-efficiency and rate classes as selection economics without invented times

competency_questions.question: Which regulated-claim classes (vermeil, gold plated, nickel release, karat marking) constrain this selection, and what may I honestly promise the customer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANCE_CLASS_FLAGS names the regulated term classes with the verify-jurisdiction rule, and CAPABILITY_HONESTY ties the achievable promise to the selected family, thickness class and color mechanism — never representing plated goods as solid gold

competency_questions.question: When should a job be referred out to PVD or refused as outside wet plating altogether?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PVD_REFERRAL_BOUNDARY lists the referral triggers (non-conductive substrate without metallization appetite, colors wet gold cannot reach, no-wet-line constraints) and frames PVD strictly as a named out-of-scope alternative class

competency_questions.question: How is a proposed bath system proven before customer work, and what must the selection record contain at handoff?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRIAL_COUPON_QUALIFICATION requires a same-substrate-class coupon run through the full proposed stack and checked for adhesion class, hue family and measured thickness, and SELECTION_RECORD_GATE lists the record fields that must exist before handoff

competency_questions.question: What can immersion and electroless gold honestly deliver, and when is that class the right selection?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ELECTROLESS_IMMERSION_CLASS explains the self-limiting displacement ceiling and the autocatalytic thickness option as mechanisms, names its honest roles (flash tier, uniform coverage of complex shapes, metallization front-end), and WEAR_CLASS_LADDER shows why the immersion ceiling sits below every wear class

glossary.definition: The supplier's operating document for a specific commercial plating product: its make-up, operating window (temperature, pH, metal content, current density), replenishment scheme and maintenance rules. In this KB the TDS is the sole authority for setpoints; the KB itself teaches only what the parameters do.

A dedicated low-gold-metal, high-complexant bath run briefly at deliberately high current density with live entry. It exists to defeat displacement (immersion) deposition on less-noble surfaces so the first gold layer adheres, and to act as a cheap sacrificial buffer that absorbs drag-in before it reaches the expensive build bath.

The main thickness-building gold electrolyte: richer in gold, run at its TDS window to lay down the microns the wear class demands. It is the costly tank in the architecture, which is why strikes and color baths exist to protect it and spend gold sparingly around it.

A lean, often alloyed gold bath used for seconds-long final coats whose job is hue, not thickness. Alloy metal additions tune the color; because it holds little gold it is cheap to dump and remake when the hue drifts off its reference.

Gold electrodeposited from acid baths with small cobalt or nickel additions that refine the grain and roughly double-to-triple hardness versus soft gold (published handbook-class comparison). Bright as plated and wear-resistant, but brittle — it cracks if the piece is formed after plating.

High-purity 24k-class gold from alkaline cyanide or sulfite baths: the most ductile electrodeposited gold, tolerant of gentle post-plate forming, but easily scratched in service. The soft/hard choice is a wear-versus-formability trade, not a quality ranking.

Gold held in solution as a comparatively weak gold-sulfite complex, run alkaline with excess sulfite and proprietary stabilizers. It removes cyanide from the gold line at the price of finite bath life (spontaneous decomposition pressure), fussier care, and weaker strike behavior on difficult surfaces.

Displacement gold: the workpiece's own surface metal dissolves to reduce gold from solution, so the reaction self-terminates once gold covers the surface. The mechanism imposes a thickness ceiling in the sub-two-tenths-of-a-micron class — color, not wear plate.

A non-gold bath in the stack — nickel, copper or palladium class — that does structural work under the gold: activation on passive metals, leveling and brightness, diffusion and corrosion barriers, or a nickel-free compliance path for skin-contact goods.

The service-duty tier a piece is plated for — decorative flash, everyday 'gold plated' thickness class, micron plating, heavy/vermeil-class — expressed against published marking-class thresholds that must be verified in the selling jurisdiction before any claim.

nodes.definition: Capture what the job actually demands before any chemistry is discussed: what metal the piece is (or claims to be), what wear duty the plated surface will see (a pendant back versus a daily-worn ring shank), the hue and karat look the customer expects and against what reference, whether the piece will be bent, sized or stone-set after plating, how many pieces the run is, whether the item touches skin for long periods (nickel-release exposure), which market it sells into, and what the customer believes they are buying. Every downstream selection decision — family, roles, support stack, claims — is a function of this profile, and a bench that names a bath before completing it is guessing.

included: substrate identity as declared and to-be-verified
wear class and service duty
color/karat target and reference
post-plate forming intent
quantity and batch shape
skin-contact and market context
customer expectation on the record
excluded: physical substrate testing and triage (surface-prep specialist)
quoting and pricing mechanics (plating-business specialist)

pros.claim: A complete profile turns bath selection from taste into a determined mapping
pros.example: a brass bangle, daily wear, rich yellow, no post-forming, EU customer resolves almost mechanically to a hard-gold wear coat over barrier with a nickel-release check

cons.claim: Customers often cannot answer the profile questions, so the bench must translate vague wants into technical fields
cons.example: the customer says 'make it look like my old ring' — someone must still decide hue family, karat look and wear class from that sentence

failure_modes: selecting a family from the piece's appearance while the substrate declaration is wrong
omitting the forming question and discovering post-plate sizing after a brittle hard-gold coat is on
leaving the skin-contact question blank so the nickel-release flag never fires
acceptance_tests: the profile sheet carries substrate, wear class, color/karat target with reference, forming sequence, quantity, skin-contact/market context and customer expectation, each filled or explicitly marked unknown-and-blocking
revisit_triggers: the customer changes the wear expectation, forming plan or market mid-job
substrate verification by the prep bench contradicts the declared metal

base.update_signal: a logged selection failure traces back to a profile field that was missing or wrong

nodes.definition: Bind every selection to the technical data sheet of a specific purchased commercial product. The doctrine has three teeth: (1) operating windows — temperature, pH, gold content, current density, additive dosing — are read from the product's TDS, never from memory, a forum, or another product's sheet; (2) this KB and the specialist teach what each parameter class does and may cite published handbook-class ranges only as ranges, so a number in this KB is never a setpoint; (3) a solution with no TDS (unlabeled bargain chemistry, a decanted mystery bottle, anything self-compounded from raw salts) is not selectable at any price, because a bath without a window cannot be controlled, replenished or defended. Choosing a family therefore always means choosing a named commercial product inside that family.

included: TDS as setpoint authority
parameter mechanisms and handbook-class ranges cited as ranges
commercial-product-only rule
rejection of TDS-less solutions
excluded: running the analysis that checks a bath against its window (sibling analysis KB)
supplier price negotiation

pros.claim: TDS-first selection makes every later control and troubleshooting step possible, because the window exists in writing
pros.example: when a deposit dulls three weeks in, the bench can compare measured pH against the product sheet instead of arguing about remembered numbers

cons.claim: Committing to one supplier's product system creates real lock-in, especially for stabilized sulfite chemistry
cons.example: a sulfite gold and its paired replenisher and stabilizer come as one closed system; switching suppliers later means requalifying the whole stack

failure_modes: quoting or promising a job from handbook numbers before the actual product's TDS is in hand
mixing one supplier's replenisher into another supplier's bath because the chemistries 'look the same'
accepting a customer-supplied no-name solution to save money
acceptance_tests: every candidate bath in a selection names a commercial product with its TDS on file, and no numeric window appears in the selection record except by TDS reference or as an explicitly labeled handbook-class range
revisit_triggers: a supplier revises, discontinues or replaces a product or its TDS
a proposed selection cannot name a TDS for one of its tanks

base.update_signal: a supplier TDS revision, product discontinuation, or a job where no TDS could be produced for a proposed tank

nodes.definition: Screen the shop, not just the job: each gold family carries a hazard tier, and a family whose tier the shop is not equipped for is off the selection menu no matter how well it fits technically. Cyanide-bearing families (alkaline cyanide golds, and acid golds whose gold is still a cyanide complex with a hard pH floor below which hydrogen cyanide evolves) demand the readiness classes as content: physical and procedural segregation of cyanide and acid tanks, storage and drains that never meet, ventilation and gas monitoring, locked labeled storage, formal operator training, emergency readiness, and a jurisdiction check on purchase and possession licensing. Sulfite chemistry sits in a lower acute tier but still forbids acid contact (sulfur dioxide release) and hardened sulfite variants re-import serious toxics via arsenic- or thallium-class dopants. This node points to formal training and jurisdiction rules; it never substitutes for them, and it never lets an unready shop improvise a procedure.

included: hazard tier per family as a selection input
readiness obligation classes (segregation, storage, labeling, ventilation and monitoring, training, emergency readiness)
the never-mix cyanide/acid line
jurisdiction licensing check pointer
excluded: day-to-day safety operations and drills (safety-compliance specialist)
waste characterization and disposal routing (safety-compliance specialist)

pros.claim: Gating the menu by readiness prevents the worst selection error a bench can make: committing to chemistry it cannot lawfully or safely run
pros.example: a shop with one room, one drain and no gas monitoring strikes alkaline cyanide golds off its menu before a customer conversation ever starts

cons.claim: The gate shrinks technical options and can force a second-best deposit for the job
cons.example: a heavy-wear ring that ideally wants a cyanide-route hard gold gets a sulfite system plus thickness compensation because the shop is cyanide-unready

failure_modes: treating cyanide readiness as a paperwork detail to catch up on after the job is quoted
assuming acid hard gold is 'not really cyanide' and skipping the tier check
adding an arsenic-hardened sulfite product without recognizing it as a hazmat upgrade decision
acceptance_tests: the family menu for the shop lists each family with its hazard tier and a readiness verdict, cyanide-tier families appear only with segregation, storage, ventilation/monitoring, training and jurisdiction-check classes verified, and the cyanide/acid never-mix line is stated on the menu itself
revisit_triggers: the shop gains or loses a readiness class (training lapses, a segregated zone is rebuilt, monitoring is installed)
a jurisdiction changes licensing or possession rules for cyanide or dopant chemistry

base.update_signal: a readiness class changes state in the shop or a jurisdiction rule governing cyanide or dopant chemistry changes

nodes.definition: Fix which rung of the published thickness ladder the job is being plated to, because the rung constrains every later choice. The ladder runs from decorative flash (a color coat measured in hundredths of a micron, months of wear at best), through the 'gold electroplate' marking class, micron plating, up to heavy and vermeil-class coats — each a published marking-class threshold referenced as a class, with current numeric limits verified in the selling jurisdiction. The rung decides whether a build bath is needed at all, whether hard gold's wear resistance matters, whether an immersion system is even eligible (its ceiling sits below every wear rung), and what the customer may be promised. A bench that plates without naming the rung cannot price the gold, size the tank time, or defend the claim.

included: the flash-to-heavy/vermeil ladder as marking classes
rung selection per service duty
the rung's consequences for family, roles and claims
excluded: measuring delivered thickness (quality-finish specialist)
asserted numeric thresholds as fact — classes carry a verify-jurisdiction flag

pros.claim: Naming the rung early converts vague durability talk into a checkable target
pros.example: 'should last daily wear' becomes a micron-class target the coupon's XRF reading can later be held against

cons.claim: The ladder tempts over-specification, spending gold the job's real duty never needed
cons.example: a display-case brooch plated to heavy-wear thickness because thicker felt safer, doubling gold cost for no service benefit

failure_modes: selling flash-class work under a marking term whose class threshold it cannot meet
selecting the family before the rung, then discovering the family cannot reach the rung economically
acceptance_tests: every selection names its ladder rung as a marking-class reference with a verify-jurisdiction flag, and the rung is consistent with the profiled service duty
revisit_triggers: a marking-class threshold changes in a selling jurisdiction
the profiled service duty changes after the rung was set

base.update_signal: a jurisdiction revises a marking-class threshold or a duty-versus-rung mismatch surfaces on a finished job

nodes.definition: Know the alkaline cyanide family as the reference gold chemistry every alternative is benchmarked against: gold held as the extremely stable aurocyanide complex, run strongly alkaline with excess free cyanide, depositing near-pure 24k-class soft gold at very high cathode efficiency (published chemistry). Its selection strengths are deposit purity and the richest standard yellow, the most ductile gold coat available (the family for gentle post-forming needs), forgiving long-lived bath behavior, and the strongest strike variants for difficult surfaces. Its selection liabilities are the top hazard tier — free cyanide with a hard alkalinity floor below which lethal gas evolves — which demands the full readiness class set, and softness in service: an unhardened coat scratches and burnishes on daily-wear surfaces. Color variants of this family (lean, alloyed flash baths) are the classic route to tuned decorative hues.

included: what the family deposits and why it is the benchmark
its strike, build and color-variant roles
hazard tier and readiness consequence
when its softness disqualifies it
excluded: its in-service carbonate/contamination management (sibling lifecycle KB)
operating setpoints — TDS territory

pros.claim: The family's ductile 24k-class deposit and strong strikes solve jobs the other families struggle with
pros.example: an antique repair needing rich fine-gold color over awkward mixed solder joints leans on a cyanide strike's activation strength

cons.claim: Its hazard tier makes it the most expensive family to be allowed to run
cons.example: segregated zones, monitoring, training and licensing overhead exist before the first gram of gold deposits, which many small benches cannot justify

failure_modes: selecting the family in a shop that fails the readiness gate
promising daily-wear durability from an unhardened soft-gold coat
treating the color-variant flash as a thickness builder
acceptance_tests: any selection of this family cites the readiness verdict from the hazard gate and a named commercial product with TDS, and pairs soft-gold selections with a wear-class justification
revisit_triggers: the shop's cyanide readiness verdict changes
a job profile shifts from formability-led to wear-led mid-selection

base.update_signal: corpus or supplier evidence changes the family's role boundaries, or the shop's readiness state moves

nodes.definition: Know the acid hard gold family as the wear-layer chemistry: gold still supplied as the cyanide complex but run in an acidic citrate/phosphate-buffered electrolyte where small cobalt or nickel additions co-deposit and refine the grain, raising hardness to roughly double-or-more that of soft gold (published handbook-class comparison) while staying bright as plated. It is the natural selection for ring shanks, bracelets and anything abraded daily, and the same chemistry class serves industrial connector plating. Selection liabilities: the deposit is brittle — post-plate forming cracks it, which makes form-first mandatory; cathode efficiency is low, so tank time per micron is long compared with the soft families; the hardener choice matters (nickel-hardened deposits put nickel into the gold layer itself, colliding with hypoallergenic intent); and although free cyanide is negligible in the window, the complex still forbids strong acidification and keeps the family inside cyanide-tier handling discipline.

included: hardened-deposit mechanism and wear-class fit
form-first consequence
cobalt versus nickel hardener as a selection fork
its hazard posture (cyanide complex at acid pH, hard pH floor)
excluded: its pH/hardener drift control in service (sibling analysis KB)
current-density delivery mechanics (process-execution specialist)

pros.claim: It is the only family whose deposit honestly supports a daily-wear scratch-resistance story at thin thickness
pros.example: a wedding-band refresh that must survive keys and desk edges selects a cobalt-hardened coat over barrier nickel rather than any soft gold

cons.claim: Brittleness plus low efficiency make it the wrong default for everything that is not wear-led
cons.example: choosing it for a filigree pendant that will be gently adjusted after plating produces microcracks at every bend

failure_modes: selecting it for a piece that will be formed, sized or burnished after plating
choosing a nickel-hardened variant for skin-contact goods without firing the nickel-release flag
assuming soft-family tank times when scheduling because the efficiency class was ignored
acceptance_tests: every selection of this family records the form-first confirmation, the hardener choice with its compliance consequence, and a named commercial product with TDS
revisit_triggers: the job's forming plan changes after selection
a hypoallergenic or nickel-free requirement appears on the profile

base.update_signal: supplier evidence or logged jobs shift the family's wear-versus-brittleness boundary or hardener guidance

nodes.definition: Know the sulfite (and mixed sulfite-thiosulfate) family as the cyanide-free path: gold held in a comparatively weak sulfite complex, run alkaline with excess ligand and proprietary stabilizers, depositing high-purity, low-stress, ductile soft gold at high efficiency. It is the default recommendation for benches that cannot or will not carry cyanide readiness, and its deposit is the one gold class with a defensible limited plate-then-form allowance. Its honest price, which selection must budget rather than discover: the weak complex wants to disproportionate, so the bath has finite life even when idle and demands lids, mechanical-not-air agitation, continuous filtration and strict acid-drag-in paranoia (acid contact crashes gold out and releases sulfur dioxide); its strikes activate difficult surfaces less strongly than cyanide strikes, tightening prep timing; hardened variants regain wear performance only by importing arsenic- or thallium-class dopants, which is a hazmat upgrade decision, not a casual add-on; and the stabilizer package locks the shop to one supplier's system.

included: the weak-complex stability liability as a selection input
cyanide-free hazard posture and its own acid-contact line
soft ductile deposit and the limited plate-then-form allowance
hardened-variant hazmat trade
supplier lock-in
excluded: in-service sulfite titration and decomposition rescue (sibling analysis and lifecycle KBs)
operating setpoints — TDS territory

pros.claim: It removes the entire acute-cyanide tier from the gold line, which is what makes a small residential-adjacent bench lawful and insurable
pros.example: a one-room studio selects a commercial stabilized sulfite system and simply never owns cyanide, monitoring, or antidote obligations for the gold tank

cons.claim: Bath mortality is structural: the selection must carry bath replacement as a recurring consumable, not an accident
cons.example: a bench that sized a large sulfite tank for occasional work watches it decompose on the shelf between jobs, paying reclaim-and-remake for gold it never plated

failure_modes: sizing the bath to ambition instead of throughput and losing it to idle decomposition
selecting it for a heavy daily-wear surface without thickness compensation or a hardening plan
adding an arsenic-hardened variant without re-running the hazard gate
acceptance_tests: selections of this family record the bath-life-as-consumable budget line, the wear-class compensation decision for soft deposits, and the hazard re-screen whenever a hardened variant is proposed
revisit_triggers: the supplier's stabilizer or replenisher system changes
throughput changes enough to re-size the bath volume decision

base.update_signal: supplier system changes or logged bath-life experience shifts the family's economics

nodes.definition: Know the rectifier-free class honestly: immersion (displacement) gold plates by dissolving the workpiece's own surface metal, so it self-terminates once covered — a mechanistic thickness ceiling in the sub-two-tenths-of-a-micron class that no settings change can tune past (published mechanism). Autocatalytic electroless gold adds a chemical reducer to keep growing beyond the ceiling, at the price of the least stable baths in the gold room and the slowest, costliest microns. The class's honest selection roles at a jewelry bench: a budget gold-flash tier sold as flash; uniform coverage of complex, hollow or filigree geometry where electroplating's current distribution fails; and the metallization front-end (over electroless nickel) that makes non-conductive or awkward pieces electroplatable afterwards. Its standard electroless nickel-phosphorus underlayer is hard and near-zero-ductility, which bans post-coat forming outright, and over-dwelling the immersion step corrodes the nickel under the gold — the classic hidden rot behind a good-looking flash.

included: displacement self-limit and autocatalytic build as mechanisms
honest roles: flash tier, complex-geometry coverage, metallization front-end
the brittle nickel-phosphorus consequence
why the class never meets a wear rung
excluded: electroless bath loading, metal-turnover and crash management (sibling lifecycle KB territory at class level)
PVD — separate boundary node

pros.claim: It coats geometry that electroplating cannot reach evenly, with no rectifier, racks or contact points
pros.example: a hollow filigree locket interior gilds uniformly in an immersion system where a rack-plated attempt left bare shadowed zones

cons.claim: The thickness ceiling is physics, so every wear-class promise made on immersion gold is false at selection time
cons.example: a 'gold dip' refresh sold as durable plating wears to grey nickel within weeks because the coat could never exceed flash class

failure_modes: selecting immersion gold for any named wear rung
letting a piece dwell past the displacement plateau chasing thickness and rotting the nickel interface
using the class on a piece that will later be formed, over its brittle nickel-phosphorus underlayer
acceptance_tests: any selection of this class states the flash-tier promise in the record, names the geometry or metallization rationale, and carries the no-post-forming flag
revisit_triggers: a job's wear expectation rises above flash after the class was chosen
the shop adds or drops the electroless nickel front-end capability

base.update_signal: logged flash-tier jobs or metallization work shift how often the class is the right answer

nodes.definition: Understand why a separate small strike tank exists in every serious gold line: on any surface less noble than gold, a currentless or low-complexant entry lets displacement deposition throw down a smutty, non-adherent immersion film — the root cause of peeling gold. The strike defeats this with low gold metal, high complexant and deliberately high current density under live entry, laying a thin adherent first layer in seconds. Its second job is economic: being small and cheap, it absorbs drag-in contamination and adhesion duty so the expensive build bath stays clean, and it is dumped and remade freely rather than rescued. Selection consequences: every family pairs with a strike of matching chemistry class; skipping the strike is only defensible where the entering surface carries fresh compatible gold already; and cyanide-free strikes are honestly weaker on passive or difficult surfaces, which tightens the prep-to-tank timing the selection must plan for.

included: displacement-suppression mechanism
sacrificial contamination-buffer economics
strike-to-family pairing
when a strike may be skipped
live entry as a strike-class rule
excluded: strike bath dosing and remake schedules in service (sibling KBs)
electrocleaning and activation before the strike (surface-prep specialist)

pros.claim: A dedicated strike converts adhesion from luck into architecture
pros.example: nickel-barriered brass entering a cyanide strike live at high current density plates a pale adherent flash where a dead entry to the build bath would have smutted

cons.claim: It is one more heated, analyzed, gold-bearing tank that small shops are tempted to delete
cons.example: a bench that folds strike duty into its build bath watches drag-in slowly poison its most expensive solution

failure_modes: omitting the strike where displacement risk exists to save a transfer
pairing a strike from one chemistry class with a build bath that its drag-out poisons
trying to rescue a contaminated strike with additions instead of dumping the sacrificial tank
acceptance_tests: every selected stack shows a strike (or a documented fresh-gold-surface justification for skipping), the strike chemistry class matches its neighbours, and the strike is flagged sacrificial in the record
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures on coupons or work trace to the strike decision
a family change upstream invalidates the strike pairing

base.update_signal: coupon or production adhesion evidence implicating strike presence, pairing or timing

nodes.definition: Design the bath architecture as three distinct roles rather than one tank: the strike buys adhesion, the build bath buys microns, and the color (flash) bath buys the final hue in seconds from a lean, often alloyed solution. A job maps onto the roles it actually needs: a flash-only fashion piece may run strike-plus-color with no build; a heavy-wear ring runs strike, long build, and often a thin color coat to hit the hue the build family cannot give; a same-color build may skip the color tank entirely. The architecture also encodes the economics — hue lives in the cheapest tank, thickness in the costliest — and the control logic: color is corrected by trimming or remaking the lean flash, never by bending the build bath off its TDS window. Selecting a system therefore means writing down which roles exist for this job, which family fills each, and which are deliberately absent.

included: role definitions and their separable economics
job-to-role mapping including deliberate absences
hue-in-the-lean-tank principle
excluded: underplate and barrier stack design in execution detail (process-execution specialist)
color drift monitoring in service (sibling analysis KB)

pros.claim: Role separation lets one build bath serve many hues, multiplying the menu without multiplying gold inventory
pros.example: one soft-gold build tank feeds rose, yellow and pale jobs by finishing each in a different lean color flash

cons.claim: Each extra role adds a transfer, and every transfer is a staining or passivation opportunity if timing slips
cons.example: a piece dried between build and color flash shows a faint stain line no buffing removes

failure_modes: using the color flash as a thickness builder because it is cheap
retuning the build bath to chase a hue the color role should own
leaving the role map implicit so the next operator guesses the sequence
acceptance_tests: the selection record names each role as present-with-family-and-product or deliberately absent, and hue responsibility is assigned to a lean tank whenever the build family cannot meet the hue target
revisit_triggers: the hue target moves outside what the assigned color role can reach
the wear rung changes, adding or deleting the build role

base.update_signal: jobs repeatedly needing a role the standard map lacks, or transfers repeatedly causing defects

nodes.definition: Control color as chemistry, not luck: electrodeposited gold hue is set by what co-deposits with the gold. Copper additions pull the coat toward pink and rose; silver pulls toward green golds; nickel pulls pale and whitish; cobalt hardeners tint slightly toward rose; and a pure deposit gives the rich standard yellow of fine gold. Two consequences matter at selection. First, every alloying addition lowers the effective karat of the coating itself — a rose flash is not a 24k coat, whatever sits beneath it — which feeds the karat story told to the customer and any karat-marked claim. Second, hue precision belongs in the lean color role where alloy ratios are cheap to trim or remake; exact commercial hue recipes are proprietary supplier products chosen by TDS and matched against a retained reference, not compounded at the bench. The underplate also shows through thin coats, so the same flash reads differently over bright nickel than over yellowed old gold — hue is a stack property, not a bath property alone.

included: alloy-direction map (copper rose, silver green, nickel pale, cobalt slight rose, pure rich yellow)
effective-karat consequence of alloying
hue as a stack property including underplate show-through
proprietary hue recipes selected by TDS
excluded: lighting-consistent color evaluation and customer color acceptance (quality-finish specialist)
in-service hue drift as a bath-health signal (sibling analysis KB)

pros.claim: Knowing the alloy directions lets the bench translate a customer hue word into a purchasable bath class
pros.example: 'champagne, not brassy' maps to a pale nickel- or silver-shifted flash class rather than another round of trial dips

cons.claim: Alloyed hues age and wear differently than pure gold, so a perfect day-one match can drift apart in service
cons.example: a copper-shifted rose flash on a daily-wear bangle warms further as the thin coat wears and the underplate ghosts through

failure_modes: selling an alloyed color coat under the karat of the build layer beneath it
chasing a hue by altering the build bath instead of assigning a color role
matching hue on a different underplate than the production stack
acceptance_tests: every hue target in a selection names its alloy direction and effective-karat consequence, and the coupon that proves it carries the production stack's underplate
revisit_triggers: the customer's hue reference changes
the underplate class changes beneath an approved hue

base.update_signal: a supplier hue-product change or a logged mismatch between coupon hue and production hue

nodes.definition: Select the non-gold tanks as deliberately as the gold: support baths do the structural work the gold cannot. Nickel class: the standard barrier and leveler under thin gold — bright nickel for mirror leveling that makes thin gold look premium, sulfamate nickel for low-stress ductility when the piece will be formed — and always carrying the nickel-release compliance flag for skin-contact goods (a published migration-limit class; verify current rules in the selling jurisdiction). Copper class: strikes that seal and make awkward substrates plateable (the classic route onto zinc die-cast) and leveling builds that smooth porous or scratched surfaces cheaply before precious metal. Palladium class: the nickel-free barrier for hypoallergenic stacks and a diffusion block in its own right, bought as a commercial system like everything else. The selection rule: the substrate and compliance context name the support classes required; the gold family then rides on a correct stack rather than compensating for a wrong one.

included: nickel bright-versus-sulfamate fork and the nickel-release flag
copper strike and leveling roles
palladium as nickel-free barrier class
substrate-and-compliance-driven support selection
excluded: underplate thickness delivery and execution (process-execution specialist)
asserted numeric release limits — flagged as verify-jurisdiction classes

pros.claim: The right support stack is the biggest wear-life and appearance lever thin gold has
pros.example: the bright-nickel-then-thin-gold trick delivers a premium mirror look from a modest gold spend on a brass locket

cons.claim: Nickel's virtues drag its allergy and compliance liabilities into every skin-contact selection
cons.example: a bright-nickel-leveled ring headed to an EU customer forces either a verified release-compliance path or a redesign onto palladium

failure_modes: defaulting to bright nickel under a piece that will be formed, embrittling the stack
omitting the copper strike on zinc die-cast and watching the stack blister
treating palladium as exotic and pricing skin-contact jobs onto nickel without the compliance check
acceptance_tests: every selected stack names its support classes with the job reason for each, skin-contact selections show the nickel-release decision (nickel-free class or verified compliance path), and forming jobs justify any bright deposit in the stack
revisit_triggers: a skin-contact or forming requirement appears after the stack was drafted
a jurisdiction changes a release-limit class the stack relies on

base.update_signal: a release-limit class change, a supplier support-product change, or logged stack failures implicating support choice

nodes.definition: Map the verified substrate class to the stack it demands, because substrate physics vetoes wishes. Bare steel never meets gold directly: iron displaces gold as a non-adherent smut while dissolving iron poisons the bath — steel takes a copper or nickel strike, then a nickel barrier, then gold. Stainless is passive: nothing adheres without a Wood's-nickel-class activation strike breaking the oxide film. Copper and brass plate readily but bleed into thin gold by diffusion over time, dulling color — a barrier earns its keep. Silver is a special migration case: under thin gold it tarnish-creeps and diffuses, so vermeil-class work still wants a barrier between silver and gold. Zinc die-cast is the fragile class: reactive, porous, dissolved by the wrong chemistry, it survives only via its cyanide-or-alkaline copper-strike route before anything else. The match also selects between gold families' tolerance: the alkaline sulfite family forgives an accidental steel touch that an acid bath would punish with immersion deposits and iron pickup.

included: substrate-class-to-stack mapping (steel, stainless, copper/brass, silver, zinc die-cast)
displacement and diffusion mechanisms as the reasons
family tolerance differences per substrate
excluded: verifying what the substrate actually is (surface-prep specialist's triage)
executing the activation and barrier layers (process-execution specialist)

pros.claim: Substrate-first selection eliminates the whole adhesion-failure class that dominates plating rework
pros.example: recognizing a 'silver' bracelet as nickel-silver (a copper alloy) reroutes the stack to barrier-then-gold before the bath had a chance to prove it wrong

cons.claim: Correct stacks for hard substrates add tanks and steps that tempt shortcuts on cheap work
cons.example: the full copper-strike route on a pot-metal belt buckle can cost more than the buckle, inviting a doomed direct attempt

failure_modes: plating gold over passive stainless without an activation strike and shipping a peel-in-the-box failure
putting thin gold straight on brass and fielding a color-fade complaint months later
letting bare steel into an acid gold tank and poisoning it with iron
acceptance_tests: every selection maps the verified substrate class to its named activation, barrier and strike requirements before a family is committed, and substrate classes outside the shop's stack capability are refused or referred
revisit_triggers: prep-bench verification reclassifies the substrate
a new substrate class starts arriving in volume (for example plated zinc castings)

base.update_signal: an adhesion or diffusion failure on work or coupon traceable to the substrate-to-stack mapping

nodes.definition: Settle, before selecting a family, whether the piece will be mechanically worked after plating — bent, sized, hammered, burnished, stone-set with prong pushing — because deposit ductility divides the families into camps. Cobalt- or nickel-hardened acid gold is brittle (elongation well under the soft classes, published characteristic): post-plate forming microcracks it, the cracks expose nickel and base metal, and no heat trick fixes it. The electroless class's nickel-phosphorus underlayer is worse. Soft golds — alkaline cyanide and especially low-stress sulfite deposits — are the one class with a limited, radius-respecting plate-then-form allowance over a ductile sulfamate-nickel underplate. The default production order for anything wear-led is therefore form first, plate second; a job that insists on post-plate work either moves to a soft-gold selection with a disclosed softer surface, or the workflow is redesigned so forming precedes the tank. Writing this decision down at selection prevents the single most expensive class of rework: stripping a cracked stack off a finished customer piece.

included: the ductility divide across families and underplates
form-first default and the soft-gold allowance with its conditions
the decision as a recorded selection input
excluded: mechanical forming technique itself (bench jewelry work)
adhesion-versus-cohesion failure reading on finished pieces (quality-finish specialist)

pros.claim: Deciding the sequence up front lets wear-led jobs keep hard gold by simply reordering work
pros.example: sizing the ring before it enters the tanks lets a cobalt-hardened coat go on last and stay crack-free

cons.claim: The form-first default collides with trade reality, where sizing requests routinely arrive after plating
cons.example: a retailer returns a plated ring for a half-size stretch, forcing a strip-and-replate quote nobody enjoys delivering

failure_modes: selecting hard gold with post-plate sizing still on the job sheet
granting the soft-gold forming allowance over a bright embrittled underplate
leaving the sequence implicit so the goldsmith forms a piece the plater assumed finished
acceptance_tests: every selection records a form-first or plate-then-form verdict, brittle-family selections carry a no-post-forming confirmation, and any plate-then-form verdict names the soft family and ductile underplate that make it defensible
revisit_triggers: post-plate mechanical work is requested after the selection verdict
the underplate class changes beneath a granted forming allowance

base.update_signal: a cracked-coat rework traced to sequence, or a job-flow change that moves forming relative to plating

nodes.definition: Compare families by how fast and how efficiently they turn tank time into microns, as classes rather than invented times. The soft families — alkaline cyanide and sulfite — run near-complete cathode efficiency, so deposition time per micron follows Faraday arithmetic closely and thickness tracks ampere-minutes almost linearly. Acid hard gold runs at a substantially lower efficiency class that falls further with bath age and current density, so the same micron costs multiples of the tank time and the rate must be verified by measurement on the first article, never assumed. The electroless class trades rate for uniformity: autocatalytic gold crawls at the slowest microns in the room. Selection consequences: batch shape and deadline interact with the rate class (a hundred-piece barrel job on a low-efficiency family may miss its date on arithmetic alone); rate-class knowledge prices tank time honestly; and any actual minutes-per-micron figure for a quote comes from the product TDS and the shop's own logged, measured runs — not from this KB.

included: efficiency and rate class comparison across families
Faraday-based estimation as a mechanism verified by measurement
batch-and-deadline interaction with rate class
excluded: delivering current density and verifying thickness on the day (process-execution specialist)
invented minutes-per-micron quotes stated as fact

pros.claim: Rate-class awareness stops the classic scheduling lie of quoting soft-gold timelines for hard-gold work
pros.example: a micron-class hard-gold batch is scheduled at a multiple of the sulfite line's tank time instead of promising the same afternoon

cons.claim: Class-level comparison invites false precision the moment someone converts it to minutes without measuring
cons.example: a quote built on a remembered efficiency figure misses badly when the aging bath's real efficiency has slid

failure_modes: scheduling a low-efficiency family as if thickness were linear in time at the soft-gold rate
letting throughput pressure flip the family choice without re-running the hazard and wear logic
quoting tank time from this KB instead of TDS plus logged measured runs
acceptance_tests: selections that commit to deadlines name the family's efficiency class and the measurement step (first-article verification) that will true up the estimate
revisit_triggers: measured first-article thickness contradicts the rate assumption
batch size or deadline changes enough to re-open the family choice

base.update_signal: logged measured runs diverge from the class-level rate expectations used in selection

nodes.definition: Cost a candidate selection by two mechanisms the invoice hides: gold capital and bath mortality. Gold capital: a bath locks up volume times gold concentration before the first piece plates — a modest build tank holds tens of grams of gold as inventory, which is why strikes and color baths are deliberately lean and why bath volume is sized to real throughput, not ambition. Bath mortality: families die differently. Alkaline cyanide baths are long-lived workhorses; sulfite baths age even idle and carry replacement as a scheduled consumable; immersion golds die by the nickel their own displacement reaction dissolves into them; electroless nickel retires on metal turnovers. The selection consequence is a per-family cost shape — high-readiness-overhead-but-durable versus low-entry-but-recurring — that belongs in the decision record as mechanism and class, never as invented prices. What happens to a dying bath (regenerate, reclaim, replace) is the lifecycle KB's territory; here the expected life class is only a selection input.

included: volume-times-concentration gold-capital mechanism
lean-tank and right-sizing logic
per-family bath-life class as a selection input
cost-shape comparison without invented figures
excluded: regenerate-versus-replace decisions and gold recovery from spent solutions (sibling lifecycle KB)
job pricing and quoting (plating-business specialist)

pros.claim: Inventory-aware selection right-sizes tanks so gold works instead of sitting
pros.example: a low-volume bench selects a small sulfite bath matched to monthly throughput rather than a prestige-sized tank that decomposes half-idle

cons.claim: Lean sizing cuts headroom, and an undersized bath depletes faster and burns deposits at normal current
cons.example: a strike sized too small for a barrel batch runs its gold down mid-run and starts plating brown

failure_modes: comparing families on chemistry price while ignoring locked gold capital
sizing a mortality-prone bath to ambition and paying for idle decomposition
writing invented currency figures into the selection record instead of mechanisms and classes
acceptance_tests: the selection record states each tank's gold-capital mechanism (volume and concentration class per TDS) and the family's bath-life class, with no invented monetary figures
revisit_triggers: throughput shifts enough to re-size tanks
logged bath-life experience contradicts the class assumed at selection

base.update_signal: gold price movement, throughput change, or logged bath-life data that reshapes the cost comparison

nodes.definition: Attach the regulated-claim flags to the selection before anything is promised or labeled. The flags are classes, each with a verify-current-rules-in-your-jurisdiction pointer: 'gold plated' and 'gold electroplate' as thickness-threshold marking classes; 'vermeil' as a class that binds substrate (sterling silver) and a heavy thickness rung together — no silver, no vermeil, whatever the coat; 'gold filled' and 'rolled gold' as mechanically-clad classes that no bath can produce, so a plating bench must never accept a job specifying them as if plating could; karat markings that must describe the coating honestly where alloyed flashes lower effective karat; and the nickel-release migration-limit class that fires whenever a nickel underplate or nickel-hardened gold sits in a skin-contact stack. This node flags claims and constrains selection; it approves nothing — final claim sign-off is a human, jurisdiction-checked act, and health questions route to professional care.

included: marking-term classes and what each binds (thickness, substrate, cladding, karat)
the nickel-release flag as a stack trigger
verify-jurisdiction discipline
flag-not-approve posture
excluded: asserted numeric thresholds as fact
advertising copy and final label approval (safety-compliance specialist and human sign-off)

pros.claim: Firing the flags at selection is the cheapest moment to be legal
pros.example: the vermeil flag kills a brass-based 'vermeil' order at the quote stage instead of at a trading-standards complaint

cons.claim: Class-level flags without current numbers force an extra verification step per market before commitment
cons.example: a batch selling into two jurisdictions needs the current thickness and release thresholds looked up twice before the record closes

failure_modes: accepting a 'gold filled' repair as a plating job because the term sounded like plating
recording a karat claim from the build bath while an alloyed flash tops the stack
skipping the nickel-release flag because the gold 'covers' the nickel
acceptance_tests: every selection lists the fired claim flags with their class basis and a verify-jurisdiction note, and no selection carrying an unresolved flag reaches the record gate
revisit_triggers: a marking or release rule changes in a selling jurisdiction
the stack changes in a way that fires or clears a flag

base.update_signal: a regulation-class change in a selling jurisdiction or a claim dispute on shipped work

nodes.definition: Translate the selected system into what may honestly be promised, and say it before the customer commits. The selected family, thickness rung and color mechanism jointly determine the truthful sentence: plated goods are never represented as solid gold; a soft-gold selection discloses that the surface scratches and burnishes in daily wear; a flash or immersion selection discloses months-not-years color life; an alloyed rose or green flash discloses its effective-karat reality alongside its hue; a hard-gold micron selection may honestly claim daily-wear scratch resistance and nothing more heroic; and heirloom or sentimental pieces carry the added disclosure that replating is a maintenance cycle, not a permanent restoration. Wear-life is stated as an expectation class tied to use, never a guaranteed figure. Where honest capability falls short of what the customer wants, the selection loops back — a different family, a different rung, or a declined job — rather than closing the gap with words.

included: capability-to-promise translation per family and rung
mandatory disclosures (not solid gold, softness, flash life, effective karat, replate cycle)
wear expectations as classes not guarantees
loop-back when capability misses the want
excluded: intake paperwork and signed acknowledgments (plating-business specialist)
post-delivery dispute handling

pros.claim: Selection-time honesty converts the biggest complaint generator in plating into a sales conversation
pros.example: a customer told at quote time that a rose flash on a daily ring will warm and wear chooses the thicker option — or accepts the cheaper one knowingly

cons.claim: Honest disclosure loses jobs to benches that promise more
cons.example: the shop that will not call a flash 'durable gold plating' watches the order go to one that will

failure_modes: letting the karat of the build layer stand in for the alloyed surface the customer sees
promising wear-life figures to close a sale
disclosing softness after the piece is plated instead of before
acceptance_tests: every selection produces a written promise set (what the surface is, how it wears as a class, what it must never be called) consistent with family, rung and hue mechanism, delivered before work is authorized
revisit_triggers: the selection changes family, rung or hue after the promise set was issued
a complaint pattern shows a disclosure was routinely misread

base.update_signal: a complaint or dispute pattern implicating a promise the selected system could not keep

nodes.definition: Recognize the jobs wet gold plating should not own and name the alternative class without pretending expertise in it. Referral triggers: non-conductive substrates (glass, ceramic, most plastics) where the customer has no appetite for the metallization front-end; finishes wet gold chemistry does not produce (the blacks, greys and rainbow interference tones of nitride and carbide coatings); volume hardware programs where dry-coating economics dominate; and constraints that exclude a wet line entirely (no drain, no chemistry storage, heat-sensitive assemblies). For these, PVD — physical vapor deposition, the vacuum dry-coating class — is the named out-of-scope alternative this bench refers to, not a process it designs, parameters, or quotes. The boundary keeps the specialist honest in both directions: it does not stretch wet chemistry onto jobs that will fail, and it does not bluff dry-coating advice it is not grounded in. A referral is a recorded selection outcome, equal in dignity to a bath choice.

included: referral trigger list
PVD named strictly as an alternative class
referral as a recorded outcome
excluded: PVD process design, parameters, vendors or quoting
metallization front-end execution (electroless class covers its selection role)

pros.claim: A clean referral boundary protects the bench's credibility and the customer's money simultaneously
pros.example: a wine-glass gilding inquiry leaves with a competent explanation and a dry-coating referral instead of a doomed wet experiment on glass

cons.claim: Referrals surrender revenue and can leak repeat customers to the referred shop
cons.example: the hardware batch sent to a PVD house takes its occasional wet-plating orders along with it

failure_modes: accepting a non-conductive piece on optimism and discovering the metallization appetite mid-job
improvising PVD advice because the customer asked
leaving referrals unrecorded so the same doomed inquiry is re-litigated monthly
acceptance_tests: each referral names its trigger, states PVD (or another class) strictly as an out-of-scope alternative, and is recorded as the selection outcome for the job
revisit_triggers: the shop adds a metallization front-end that converts a referral class into an in-scope stack
referral volume in one class suggests a capability decision

base.update_signal: a capability change (metallization front-end) or a referral-volume pattern worth a build-versus-refer decision

nodes.definition: Prove the proposed selection on metal before it touches a customer piece: run a coupon of the same substrate class through the entire proposed stack — prep hand-off state, strike, support layers, build, color flash, in the planned sequence and transfers — and judge it against the selection's own targets. The coupon answers three questions measurement can answer: does the stack adhere (a bend-and-tape-class check appropriate to the goods, reading peel as reject while distinguishing hard gold's intrinsic crack behavior), does the hue land in the intended family against the retained reference on the same underplate, and does measured thickness (XRF or equivalent method class) reach the declared rung in the planned tank time. First-run stacks, changed suppliers, changed hue targets and irreplaceable customer pieces always earn a coupon; a repeat job on a logged, previously qualified stack may cite its history instead. This is selection qualification, not routine bath surveillance — the sibling analysis KB owns the bath's day-to-day windows.

included: same-substrate-class coupon through the full stack
adhesion, hue-family and measured-thickness checks as method classes
when a coupon is mandatory versus citable history
excluded: routine in-service bath analysis and drift monitoring (sibling analysis KB)
final customer color acceptance (quality-finish specialist)

pros.claim: The coupon converts selection from argument to evidence at the cost of one small plate
pros.example: a proposed rose-over-nickel stack shows a distinctly warmer hue on the coupon than the reference, so the flash product changes before a single earring is risked

cons.claim: Coupons cost time and gold, and deadline pressure argues loudly against them
cons.example: a same-day trade job tempts the bench to treat the customer's piece as its own coupon

failure_modes: qualifying on a convenient brass coupon for a zinc die-cast production run
skipping the coupon on a first-run stack because the individual products are familiar
reading hard gold's intrinsic bend cracking as an adhesion failure and discarding a sound selection
acceptance_tests: before first production, a coupon of the work's substrate class has passed adhesion class, hue family versus the retained reference on the production underplate, and measured thickness at the declared rung — or the record cites the prior qualified run it repeats
revisit_triggers: any element of the stack changes (product, supplier, underplate, hue target, sequence)
production results diverge from what the qualifying coupon showed

base.update_signal: a stack change or a production-versus-coupon divergence that questions the qualification

nodes.definition: Close selection with a written record that the next benches can execute and audit, and let nothing pass without it. The record names: the job profile it answers; the chosen family and the named commercial product per tank with TDS references; the role map (strike, build, color — present or deliberately absent); the support stack with its substrate and compliance reasons; the wear rung as a marking-class reference; the hue target with its alloy mechanism and effective-karat note; the form-sequence verdict; the fired compliance flags and their resolution state; the honest promise set issued to the customer; the hazard-gate verdict for every tank; and the coupon result or cited qualified history. A selection failing any element is held with the gap named — never advanced on momentum. The record is what makes a good result repeatable and a bad one diagnosable; without it the shop owns a lucky afternoon, not a process.

included: the record's required fields
hold-with-named-gap discipline
handoff to process execution
referrals recorded as outcomes
excluded: run-day parameter logging (process-execution specialist)
the bath log as an in-service evidence base (sibling analysis KB)

pros.claim: A complete record turns one success into a repeatable product
pros.example: six months later the same retailer reorders, and the bench re-runs the recorded stack and coupon citation instead of re-deriving the selection

cons.claim: The gate adds ceremony that feels heavy on small familiar jobs
cons.example: a routine flash refresh still requires its record row, which a busy bench experiences as friction

failure_modes: advancing a selection with an unresolved compliance flag because the deadline argued louder
recording the family but not the named products, making the run unrepeatable at reorder
back-filling the record after plating, which documents the guess instead of gating it
acceptance_tests: no job enters production without a record carrying every required field, holds name their missing element, and a sampled record suffices for a different operator to re-run the job without oral tradition
revisit_triggers: the downstream specialist's intake needs change what the record must carry
a repeat-job failure traces to a field the record did not capture

base.update_signal: a handoff failure or intake-contract change from the executing specialists

edges.why_related: the ladder rung is chosen for the service duty and market the profile records

cyanide-free strikes are honestly weaker, a family fact the strike role must carry into timing requirements
the three-role architecture is built around the strike's non-negotiable position at the front
the rung decides whether a build role exists at all and how heavy it runs
the classic alloyed color-flash variants that define hue control live in this family's chemistry
nickel, copper and palladium supports are commercial systems selected by TDS exactly like the golds
substrate matching can only name a stack from the support classes the shop can actually field
the declared-and-verified substrate in the profile is the input the match maps to a stack
the family's brittleness is the fact that forces the form-first default
the soft sulfite deposit is what makes the limited plate-then-form allowance exist
sulfite mortality is the bath-life class that forces life-as-consumable budgeting into selection
marking-term flags bind to the thickness rung the ladder declares
the coupon must carry the work's substrate class, which the match defines
the coupon result (or cited qualified history) is a required field of the record
the record cannot close while a fired claim flag is unresolved
the issued promise set is a required record field so the shop can later prove what was disclosed
the top-hazard-tier family appears on the menu only where the full cyanide readiness class set is verified
acid golds remain cyanide-complex chemistry with a hard pH floor and stay inside cyanide-tier handling discipline
the record may cite windows only by TDS reference or as labeled handbook-class ranges — never invented setpoints
the promise set may only use claim terms whose regulated class the selection actually satisfies
the two families compete for the same jobs from opposite corners: hard gold wins wear resistance, sulfite wins formability, hazard profile and shop accessibility
edges.resolution_rule: the profiled wear class and form-sequence verdict decide: wear-led, form-first jobs go hard gold where the shop's readiness allows; post-forming or cyanide-unready situations go soft sulfite with thickness compensation and a disclosed softer surface — and safety readiness caps the menu before either preference speaks

edges.why_related: the alloyed flash that delivers the desired hue simultaneously lowers the effective karat the customer thinks they are buying
edges.resolution_rule: disclosure wins: the hue is described together with its effective-karat reality and the coat is never marketed by the karat of the layer beneath it; if the honest description kills the sale, the selection changes rather than the description

edges.why_related: every role in the architecture is another gold-bearing, heated, maintained tank, so capital economics push toward collapsing roles the architecture says to keep separate
edges.resolution_rule: the strike is never deleted where displacement risk exists; savings come from leaning volumes (small strike, lean color flash) and right-sizing the build to throughput, and only a fresh-compatible-gold-surface justification may remove a role

edges.why_related: the self-limiting displacement ceiling mechanically fixes what an immersion selection may promise: color, not wear
each step up the thickness ladder multiplies tank time through the selected family's rate class, driving the scheduling economics

profile first, then screen the shop's readiness against what the job would demand — the menu is per-shop, the verdict per-job

when honest capability cannot meet the recorded expectation, the job profile itself is renegotiated rather than the promise inflated
